paper_metadata.title: Learning to Link with Wikipedia
paper_metadata.venue: CIKM'08 (ACM Conference on Information and Knowledge Management), Napa Valley, California, USA
paper_metadata.abstract: The paper presents a machine-learning wikification system that identifies important terms in unstructured documents and links them to the appropriate Wikipedia articles. It frames the linked concepts as structured knowledge for downstream tasks and reports approximately 75% precision and recall on Wikipedia and real-world documents.

problem_addressed: Automatically wikify unstructured text: detect the terms/topics that merit links and disambiguate each to the intended Wikipedia article. The objective is to add explanatory cross-references and thereby transform plain text into an unambiguous, structured set or graph of Wikipedia concepts.

methodology.description: Execution pipeline: (1) obtain candidate n-grams from a document and retain those above a low Wikipedia link-probability threshold; (2) disambiguate candidate anchors to Wikipedia articles using a C4.5 classifier over sense commonness, weighted semantic relatedness to unambiguous context articles, and context quality; (3) merge phrase-to-article associations into candidate topics; (4) apply a bagged C4.5 link-detector classifier to select link-worthy topics using average/max link probability, relatedness, disambiguation confidence, category-tree generality, and mention frequency, first/last occurrence, and spread; (5) create links to selected Wikipedia topics. For illustrative graph construction, extracted topics are connected when their Wikipedia link-based relatedness is significant.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: Wikipedia is the controlled target vocabulary/knowledge base: candidate phrases are resolved to Wikipedia articles. Wikipedia anchor statistics supply priors and labels; incoming/outgoing link structure supplies semantic relatedness; its category hierarchy supplies a generality feature. The paper illustrates optional connection to DBpedia/YAGO for more formal reasoning, but does not use an externally specified ontology as a mandatory extraction schema.

input_output.input_type: Plain, unstructured natural-language documents; evaluated on Wikipedia article text with markup removed and on English newswire stories.
input_output.input_granularity: Document-level processing over all n-grams and their document context; mention-level candidate anchors are aggregated to document topics.
input_output.output_representation: Selected text-to-Wikipedia-article links (disambiguated concepts/topics); optionally, a document concept graph whose nodes are extracted Wikipedia topics and whose edges denote significant Wikipedia link-based relatedness.

models_and_tools: Bagged C4.5 classifier for final link detection
Wikipedia Link-based Measure for semantic relatedness
Wikipedia anchor/link statistics and category tree
Amazon Mechanical Turk for human evaluation
datasets: Wikipedia dump released 20 November 2007, just under two million articles
700 randomly selected Wikipedia articles with at least 50 links, excluding lists and disambiguation pages: 500 training, 100 configuration, 100 final disambiguation evaluation
Separate 100 Wikipedia articles with 9,300 manually linked topics for link-detection evaluation
AQUAINT: 50 Associated Press newswire stories of 250–300 words for out-of-Wikipedia evaluation
A length-matched, link-dense set of 500 Wikipedia articles for newswire classifier training
Manually verified/corrected corpus of wikified news articles

metrics: Human majority-vote link correctness and error-category percentages
baselines: Mihalcea and Csomai (2007) Wikify link-probability detector, reported as estimated and perfect-disambiguation upper-bound combined performance
evaluation.setting: Intrinsic disambiguation evaluation used 11,000 anchors from 100 held-out Wikipedia articles. Intrinsic link-detection evaluation used 100 new Wikipedia articles and 9,300 manually linked topics after removing markup. External evaluation used 50 short Associated Press AQUAINT stories: 449 proposed links were each judged by three Mechanical Turk workers; missing links were elicited from five workers per document, with at least three votes required; the corrected corpus supplied ground truth. Candidate-generation and classifier thresholds were configured on held-out Wikipedia articles.

value: Held-out Wikipedia disambiguation: strict most-valid-sense classifier achieved recall 95.7%, precision 98.4%, and F-measure 97.1%; selecting all valid senses gave 96.6%, 97.0%, and 96.8%, respectively. The Medelyan et al. baseline scored F=92.9%; authors report a 76% error-rate reduction for strict selection.
Held-out Wikipedia link detection: new detector scored recall 73.8%, precision 74.4%, F=74.1%, versus Wikify estimated 46.5%, 49.6%, F=48.0% and upper bound 53.4%, 55.9%, F=54.6%.

External AQUAINT human-corrected evaluation: precision 76%, recall 73%, F=75%; of proposed links 76.4% were correct, 0.9% had a wrong destination, 19.8% were irrelevant/unhelpful, and 2.9% had an unknown error reason.

The disambiguator trained in 13 minutes and tested in four minutes after a three-minute load; the link detector trained in 37 minutes and tested, including disambiguation, in eight minutes on the specified desktop.

value: Author-stated: learns from abundant human-created Wikipedia links and combines sense commonness, context-relatedness, and context quality rather than using a fixed heuristic.
Author-stated: avoids part-of-speech analysis and parsing the entire Wikipedia; uses only 500 training articles, is potentially language independent, and requires lower resources.
Experimental: high held-out disambiguation F=97.1% and consistent approximately 74–75% end-task performance on Wikipedia and independently human-judged newswire.

Review-level inference: mapping ambiguous textual mentions to Wikipedia identifiers makes the output directly usable as linked entities/concepts in a later Text-to-KG workflow, unlike an ungrounded keyword list.

value: Author-reported: link detection is substantially harder and more subjective than disambiguation; performance drops from disambiguation to about F=74% for link detection.
Author-reported: the comparison with Wikify is limited because methods were developed and evaluated on different Wikipedia versions.

Author-reported: applying a classifier trained on longer encyclopedic articles to short newswire initially identified very few link-worthy topics, requiring a separately constructed length-matched training set.

Review-level inference: this is a Wikipedia-closed linking system; concepts absent from, or poorly represented in, that snapshot cannot be linked, and its target ontology/schema changes with Wikipedia.
